title: Data Architect Senior
description:
Data Architect Senior
We are seeking a Data Architect Senior to support a public sector environmental regulatory modernization initiative. This role will design and lead data integration between a regulatory system, a Databricks-based data management platform, and a geospatial platform. The focus is establishing trusted, timely, and reusable data for regulators, decision-makers, and the public. The ideal candidate will set the direction for how regulatory, environmental, and spatial data moves, connects, and is governed across these systems, working within a high-performing, multidisciplinary team in a fast-paced, agile environment.
This position requires someone who can design enterprise data architectures and lead complex system integrations to support a regulatory program. The role encompasses defining target-state data architecture across multiple platforms, designing conceptual, logical, and physical data models for regulatory and geospatial domains, and establishing integration patterns suited to each use case. Responsibilities include architecting lakehouse structures on Databricks with medallion layers and Delta Lake tables, designing spatial data flows that preserve geometry and coordinate reference systems, leading data pipeline design with data engineers and developers, defining data contracts and API specifications, resolving complex integration issues, embedding data governance practices including metadata management and lineage, ensuring compliance with government information security and privacy standards, defining data quality rules and monitoring approaches, applying role-based access controls, serving as a trusted advisor to program leadership and technical teams, coordinating with enterprise architecture and cybersecurity teams, producing architecture documentation and decision records, and mentoring team members on data architecture best practices. This role will participate in agile ceremonies and turn architecture into actionable user stories.
Qualifications

• University degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Geomatics, or a related field

•
7+ years - progressive experience in data architecture, data engineering, or data integration, with at least 3 years in a data architect role

•
3+ years - hands-on experience designing solutions on Databricks, including Delta Lake, Spark (PySpark/SQL), and Unity Catalog

•
5+ years - data modelling experience with relational, dimensional, and lakehouse approaches

•
5+ years - designing enterprise integration patterns, including REST APIs, ETL/ELT, event streaming, and change data capture

•
5+ years - cloud data platforms, preferably Microsoft Azure (Data Lake Storage, Data Factory, Event Hubs, Key Vault)

• Experience with ServiceNow Integration

•
3+ years - public sector experience, ideally with government regulatory systems or programs

•
3+ years - integrating with geospatial platforms and working knowledge of geospatial data concepts, formats, and standards

• Solid understanding of data governance, metadata management, data quality, and data security principles

•
3+ years - working in agile delivery teams in a public sector capacity

• Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences

• Demonstrated systems thinking, creative problem solving, agility, drive for results, ability to build collaborative environments, develop networks, and develop self and others

Nice to Have

• Certification in The Open Group Architecture Framework (TOGAF)

•
5+ years - designing and implementing enterprise architecture database plans and models that align an organization's data, information or technology with required business capabilities in a large enterprise IT environment

•

title: Founding Robot Operator, US
description:
Everyone should be able to afford a well-built home in a beautiful neighborhood. Our ambition is to help solve the housing crisis and bring beauty back to the places we live. We are developing robots that can make intricate, high-quality construction affordable at scale. We are hiring our founding Robot Operators in the United States, starting with our first pilot in San Antonio, Texas.

You will help bring a system already used on sites in the Netherlands and the UK to a new market. As one of our first US operators, you will help establish how we work on site and give our engineering team direct feedback from the field.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is hands-on construction work with robots. You will move bricks and mortar, keep the robots supplied, set up equipment and clean the site. You will also operate the robots using Atrium, our in-house software, and work with our engineers when something needs fixing.

No previous robotics or construction experience is required. We are looking for practical people with technical intuition, an eye for detail and the initiative to solve problems. We will train you to operate our systems. This is a full-time role. Training starts at our headquarters in Amsterdam, with costs covered by Monumental.

Our operators come from construction, retail, hospitality, events, farms, workshops and engineering. What they share is a preference for working with their hands and seeing the things they build.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Prepare construction projects: understand the build plan and assess site conditions.

- Place markers and take photos for 3D reconstruction.

- Set up and operate masonry robots using a laptop and our software.

- Carry and load bricks and mortar, move equipment and keep the work area safe and tidy.

- Help with site tasks such as cutting bricks, setting wall ties and pointing walls.

- Troubleshoot with our engineering and operations teams.

- Record problems and improvements so our engineers can develop the hardware and software.

- Work with the contractors and trades around you as the face of Monumental on site.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

- A practical, technical mindset and a willingness to learn.

- Comfort with physical work outdoors, early starts and changing site conditions.

- Attention to detail: the quality of the finished wall matters.

- Initiative when something does not go to plan.

- A valid driver’s license and comfort driving to construction sites.

- Good spoken and written English for working with our team.

- Construction, maintenance or other hands-on experience is useful, but not required.

LOCATION

This is an on-site role in San Antonio, Texas, starting with our first US pilot. You need to be able to work on construction sites in the San Antonio area. This is not a remote role.

WHY MONUMENTAL?

You will be part of the team bringing our robots to US construction sites for the first time. The work combines physical building, technical problem-solving and direct collaboration with the people developing the robots. Your feedback will help shape the next deployment.

Learn more about Monumental https://www.monumental.co/about, Atrium https://www.monumental.co/atrium and life as a Robot Operator https://www.monumental.co/blog/the-best-product-job-isnt-in-engineering.

If you do not meet every line above but enjoy building things and solving practical problems, we would still like to hear from you.

title: PhD Position: World Models for Software Architecture Synthesis (Constructor Fabric)
description:
Supervisor: Prof. Dr. Alexander Tormasov

About the Position

Constructor Knowledge Labs (CKL), in collaboration with Constructor Technology, invites applications for a PhD position in machine learning for software engineering and formal methods, on the Constructor Fabric project.

Constructor Fabric turns a company's informal knowledge into production software through a pipeline of composable capability units called gears : requirements → architecture → product fit → framework (G1) → application → runtime. We are building a World Model over that pipeline - a model that does not just generate code, but predicts the consequences of an architectural decision: total cost of ownership, unintended side effects, latency and failure behaviour, and whether a proposed composition is even admissible.

The central object is not a digital twin of the application but its formal architectural skeleton : gear contracts (GearSpec), a typed attributed hypergraph of the application (AppGraph), a composition algebra that defines which assemblies are legal, and several semantic projections (types, protocols, resources, security) over which properties are proved, refuted by counterexample, or reported as an explainable gap . All of it is written in a domain-specific language whose syntax trees and graphs we keep in a projectional editor (JetBrains MPS) - so the DSL is not a convenience layer, it is the thing that defines the model's state space and the boundary of what the model is allowed to propose.

The Assistant Lane Support Subject Matter Expert (SME) is an integral member of the West Virginia National Guard (WVNG) Ridge Runner Irregular Warfare Exercise (IWX) Program, responsible for supporting the planning, coordination, execution, and closeout of complex Special Operations Forces (SOF) training exercises. The position assists the Lane Support SME in coordinating logistics, manpower, resources, exercise infrastructure, and administrative requirements across assigned areas of operation.

The Assistant Lane Support SME must demonstrate strong organizational, logistical, asset deconfliction, and project management capabilities while supporting multiple exercises in various stages of development and execution. The position requires effective coordination with military personnel, Government agencies, civilian authorities, and domestic and international exercise participants in a dynamic, mission-driven environment.

Role and Responsibilities

• Provide operational, logistical, and administrative support to the WVNG Joint Staff Office, WVNG J37, WVNG J3 Joint Operations Center, and Ridge Runner Program in support of exercise planning, coordination, and execution.

• Support exercise lane development, site preparation, setup, execution, and recovery, including coordination with local business owners, municipal officials, and private landowners for access to facilities, infrastructure, and training locations through the Realistic Military Training (RMT) Packet process.

title: Customer Service Representative - TRADE
description:
Location: Remote (Pakistan-based)
Schedule: Monday-Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m. EST
Employment Type: Full-Time
Reports To: Trade & Commercial Principal
Position Overview
The Customer Service Rep (CSR) is the primary point of contact for all service issues on Trade & Commercial (T&C) accounts after an order is placed. The purpose of the role is to take post-sale service and administrative work off the Trade and Commercial sales representatives so they can spend their time selling. At the start of each order, the CSR emails the customer to confirm order details and introduce themselves as the point of contact for any issues going forward. From there, the role is centered on identifying, routing, and driving service issues to resolution - working with Service, Parts Sales, and Sales to get problems fixed and keeping the customer informed along the way. This is a fully remote role working United States Eastern Time business hours, with a defined path to senior service and customer success positions as the CSR builds a track record.
Key Responsibilities

• Service Request Management

• Serve as the primary point of contact for service across all Trade & Commercial accounts.

• Receive service requests from customers directly, or from sales representatives on the customer's behalf.

• Complete the customer service request form and create the corresponding case in Salesforce.

• Work with the customer to gather all information needed to action the request correctly the first time.

• Direct each request to the correct internal department (service, parts, delivery, etc.)

• Service Tracking & Customer Communication

• Monitor open service cases to ensure each is actioned by the responsible department in a timely manner.

• Generate Salesforce reports to track T&C service activity and report results back to management.

• Run the weekly customer service meeting to prioritize requests, identify issues, and solve problems.

• Communicate scheduled service dates and details to customers promptly.

• Gather customer feedback systematically for reporting and improvement purposes.

• Book Jobs & Confirm Details

• Send the order confirmation email at the start of each order to confirm order details, introduce yourself as the customer's point of contact for any issues, introduce the delivery coordinator, and communicate current lead times.

• Perform basic order QAQC review against the standard checklist before booking jobs.

• Support finance in collecting customer payment via payment link and moving orders off hold.

Qualifications
Strong English fluency, written and spoken - this is the most important requirement for the role. The CSR is the company's primary voice to the customer after the sale and speaks daily with U.S. builders, contractors, and homeowners by phone and email.
Ability to work United States Eastern Time business hours consistently, Monday through Friday.
2+ years in customer service, customer support, customer success, administrative assistant, order management, project coordination, inside sales support, or a similar role.
Highly organised, with the ability to manage a high volume of open orders and service cases without losing track of details.
Comfortable following up persistently with internal departments to hold timelines while maintaining strong working relationships.
Experience with Salesforce CRM, Microsoft Office, and Google Workspace.
Comfortable following documented processes and checklists, and documenting activity accurately.
Building products, millwork, construction, or U.S.-facing B2B account support experience preferred.
Reliable remote work setup required: a quiet, dedicated workspace; high-speed internet with a backup
connection; backup power sufficient to cover outages during scheduled hours; and a computer capable of running CRM and VoIP software.

title: Head of Investor Relations
description:
We are hiring a Head of Investor Relations to lead the team that runs our investor network.
Pairs is a vetted private capital network. We put break-out founders in front of the family offices, VCs and strategic investors who fit them, and our team runs the investor relations work around every introduction. We are paid by the founder for our work, never by the round. Investors are members of the network and pay nothing. We are a small, senior team, profitable and self-funded.
The role
This is a leadership seat. You run the IR team: around six direct reports, the associates who each hold a book of members and clients. You report directly to the two co-founders.
Your job is to make that team excellent. You hire well, set a clear bar, run the weekly rhythm, coach every associate on their calls and pitches, and have the hard conversation early when someone is off track. The team’s results are your results.
Founders work with us for our investor network. Members read what we send because it fits what they told us. Through your team, you own that network and keep every relationship getting stronger month after month. You still take the mandate calls with our most senior family offices, because a leader who stays close to the work coaches it better.
What you will own

• The IR team: around six direct reports. Hiring, onboarding, weekly 1:1s, coaching, performance, and a clear bar for what good looks like.

• The team’s rhythm: a weekly kickoff, a weekly review of every win and loss, and a team that runs on its own when you are not in the room.

• The health of the investor network: more active members every month, and every member getting deals that fit their thesis at the pace they asked for.

• Pitch quality: every introduction your team sends is one you would put your own name on.

• A weekly read on the numbers to the co-founders: mandate calls, activations, pitches, founder calls and referrals.

• Senior mandate calls with family offices and strategic investors, including new regions.

• Close work with our client success team, so every client’s raise keeps moving.

You are a fit if you

• Have run a team before, ideally around six direct reports, and can show what they achieved under you and who you grew.

• Have hired, coached and, when needed, let go of people, and held a team to a standard without doing their work for them.

• Have 6 or more years on the investment side of a family office, VC or growth fund, or in capital raising for private companies.

• Hold real, current relationships with family offices, and know what they ask before they take a founder call.

• Write a two-line pitch an investor reads to the end.

• Run on systems: CRM discipline, a clear weekly rhythm, nothing left in your head.

• Treat discretion as a reflex: founders’ numbers and members’ names stay confidential.

• Work like it is 2026: AI tooling runs the admin so your hours go to people.

What we offer
US$200K to US$300K total compensation. Fully remote, with a few hours of overlap with US Eastern time. A seat reporting directly to both co-founders, a team to lead, and a network that grows with every month you put into it.
How to apply: hit apply, which takes you to a short application form. We read every application. Please do not name investors or companies from past roles anywhere in it.
Compensation Range: $200K - $300K

title: Manager, Software Engineering - Cloud infrastructure
description:
About Pyka
Pyka’s goal is to provide society with a new form of safe, clean, and cost-effective transportation enabled by autonomous electric aviation.
To get there, we’re taking a different approach than most. We're applying our technologies to every industry where autonomous electric aircraft can be useful, starting with the highest value and most dangerous jobs. In doing so, we're building game-changing products manufactured at scale, while perfecting the safety, reliability, and capabilities of our autonomy engine and electric propulsion systems. 
We design, develop and manufacture an ecosystem of technologies including proprietary flight control software, avionics, high power density motors, motor controllers, batteries, and custom carbon-fiber composite airframes.
Today, we supply autonomous electric aircraft for cargo transport and crop protection to real-world customers across four separate continents and have secured industry-first regulatory approvals from the FAA. Our cargo aircraft enables remote connectivity, enhances express delivery networks, and ensures fast and reliable shipping of critical supplies to areas in need. Our crop protection aircraft offers agricultural services providers and farmers an autonomous tool to make aerial application safer, more precise, and less harmful to surrounding environments. Both vehicles are highly economical to operate, easy to deploy, and significantly reduce CO2 emissions in their respective industries. 
What you work on at Pyka makes people’s lives better now and brings the future of electric aviation one step closer each day. 

Role Overview
Pyka is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to be the software owner of our Dropship and Cargo programs. The software problems in these programs span the stack: path planning over long ranges, controls for a new airframe, integration of new sensors, engine control and state-of-charge management on a hybrid powertrain, and incorporating weather into how a mission is planned and flown. You will be responsible for the software behavior of these aircraft as a whole - what it needs to do, how the pieces fit together, and whether it is ready to fly - and you will be the engineer the Dropship team comes to when software is the open question on their side.
 
Some of the current and future projects you will likely contribute to include:
Path planning for long-range cargo missions that accounts for energy state, winds aloft, and weather along the route
Energy management on a hybrid powertrain: engine control, state-of-charge policy, and how the aircraft trades power against range, payload, and reserve
Flight controls and handling for a new airframe, from simulation through flight test
Integrating new sensors and payload systems, and defining the software needs before the hardware is fixed
Turning operational feedback from cargo flights into requirements for the next iteration of the aircraft
Defining what mission planning and ground tools need to expose to operators flying these aircraft

Export Control Requirements
This position requires access to technology, software and other information that is subject to governmental access control restrictions, due to export controls.  Employment in this position is conditioned on the continued availability of government authorization to authorize release of such items, to the extent required, including without limitation an export license, or other documentation required to establish authorization to receive access to such items. 
Company may delay commencement of employment, rescind an offer of employment, terminate employment, and/or may modify job responsibilities, compensation, benefits, and/or access to Company facilities and information systems, as Company deems appropriate, in order to ensure compliance with applicable government access control restrictions.

title: Global Product Manager (Remote/Full-time)
description:
ABOUT GENERATION:
At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives. We are a global nonprofit organization that supports adults to achieve economic mobility through employment. Generation trains and places adult learners of all ages into careers that are otherwise inaccessible, working in partnership with governments, employers, and other system actors. We also conduct original research and share data insights on high-priority global workforce transition topics to inform decision-making by workforce system stakeholders. Launched in 2015, Generation comprises a global hub (Generation You Employed, or GYE) and a network of in-country affiliates. To date, the network has 150,000+ graduates and 23,000+ employers across 50 professions and 17 countries.
When learners join Generation, 91% are unemployed, of which nearly half are long-term unemployed. Three months after completing our program, graduates have a 78% job placement rate, rising to 88% within six months. Of our employed graduates, 79% are hired by repeat employers who have previously hired Generation graduates, and 89% are in jobs directly related to the profession for which we have trained them. Employed graduates immediately earn an average of 3-4X their previous earnings. Two to five years after graduation, 77% of our alumni from upper-middle income countries continue to meet their daily financial needs and 63% can save for the future. To date, Generation’s global graduates have earned more than $1.9 billion in wages. Generation graduates typically have a secondary school background, 52% are female, 28% have dependents, and the majority identify with underrepresented communities in their country.
JOB OBJECTIVES:
The Global Product Manager position is focused on:

Job Summary
Granicus serves more than 7,000 public-sector agencies and powers approximately 30 billion digital interactions annually. Within the Office of the CTO, we operate an AI-native software development lifecycle: a production engineering model in which autonomous agents perform high-confidence implementation work and senior engineers orchestrate, review, and own the outcome. The model is established and operating; we are scaling it across additional delivery teams.
This role joins one of those teams. Our engineering standards are calibrated to the practices used by leading software and AI organizations - generator-verifier architecture , eval-driven development , staged deployment , and high-volume autonomous pull-request pipelines - operated within a FedRAMP-authorized environment. We are hiring practitioners who will set and uphold these standards, not engineers who simply use AI tooling.
Operating constraints (non-negotiable): agents execute only within branches; all agent-generated code passes senior human review before merging to production; autonomous execution is a force multiplier and does not transfer accountability away from the responsible engineer. Compliance obligations - NIST 800-53 Rev 5, WCAG, SOC 2, and applicable FedRAMP authorizations - are treated as engineering requirements and a source of competitive advantage.
Why this role exists
High-volume autonomous agent pipelines are straightforward to demonstrate and difficult to operate safely, performantly, and auditably at scale. This role owns that problem. It is responsible for the generator-verifier architecture, agent orchestration patterns, the eval-driven development discipline, and a continuous integration and delivery system engineered for a high volume of autonomous agent pull requests - all within a security boundary that keeps model inference inside the VPC (AWS Bedrock) and sandboxes agent actions (WASM-isolated runtime with encrypted credential storage). The role sets the engineering standards inherited by every delivery team and is the final human accountability gate before agent-generated code merges to productio
What Your Impact Will Look Like

•
Own the generator-verifier architecture - the loop in which generator agents produce changes and verifier agents, automated tests, evaluation suites, SAST/DAST, and policy checks validate them, enabling volume to scale without quality regression.

•
Define agent orchestration patterns - task decomposition, dispatch, sandboxing, and reassembly across the agent array, including secure state and credential handling via WASM-isolated runtimes and encrypted credential vaults.

description:
B2C SaaS | Subscriptions | Stripe
Location: Remote (Europe)
Employment: Full-time, B2b contract
Start date: ASAP
Our client is a global B2C SaaS company operating multiple subscription-based digital products with millions of users worldwide.
Payments are built on Stripe and PayPal and are already live in production. This role will be the first dedicated payments hire in-house. Until now, payments have been managed across Product and Business teams, with part-time advisory support from a Head of Payments.
We’re looking for a Product Owner / Payments Operations Specialist who will become the main point of ownership for payments performance and analytics across the product portfolio.

What You’ll Do

• Own and improve subscription payment performance across multiple products (authorization, retries, recovery, churn).

You won’t own regulatory compliance, but you will help spot issues early through data and payment flow analysis.
What Success Looks Like

• Payments performance is clear, measurable, and improving.

• Key metrics like authorization rate and recovery rate are understood and actively managed.

• Payment issues are identified early and resolved faster.

What We’re Looking For

• 5+ years of experience in payments operations, payments analytics, or subscription-based B2C SaaS.

• Strong hands-on experience with Stripe (subscriptions, billing, reporting, disputes).

• Solid understanding of recurring billing mechanics (auto-renewals, retries, dunning).

• Experience working with payment KPIs and turning data into actions.

• Comfortable being the first payments specialist and building structure where it didn’t exist before.

Nice to Have

• Experience in high-volume subscription products.

• Exposure to fraud / chargebacks tools (Stripe Radar, Verifi, Ethoca).

• Background as a payments owner or early hire in a payments function.

Why This Role

• First dedicated payments role in the company

• High visibility and real ownership

• Opportunity to shape how payments are handled long-term

Kong is hiring an ADR Team Lead to support our Benelux, and Nordics regions. This is a player-coach role. You'll be taking an active hand in developing the team around you, especially the newer ADRs still finding their footing.

You'll work closely with, and report into, the Senior Manager for NEMEA. You're shaping how the team operates, not running it solo. Think of this as a high-impact individual contributor role with a leadership layer built in: the natural next step for an ADR who's ready to start making other people better, not just themselves.

Our NEMEA team is already strong. Driven, independent, hitting their numbers. What they need isn't more oversight. They need someone who sharpens how the team works, especially around process and tooling, while making sure newer reps get the support to ramp fast.

You'll report to Oscar Winberg. He moves fast, sets a high bar, and expects people to bring solutions, not just flag problems. Support newer ADRs. You'll be the first point of contact for less tenured reps, helping them ramp faster and build good habits early. Sharpen process and tooling. You'll be the go-to person for best practice on Salesforce, Outreach, and the team's automation tools.

Contribute to the wider GTM motion. You'll keep strong alignment with your AE partners and take part in pipe review cadences. You'll support the Senior Manager in preparing performance updates and regional insights, and join bi-weekly RD cadences where it makes sense.

- Hands-on ADR or SDR experience. You know what this job feels like from the inside, not just what it looks like from a deck.

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refueling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service - spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

People Operations

title: Senior Risk Investigator - Fraud Incident Management & Partner Response

description:
About the Team

Mercury* is building a complete financial stack for startups, and Risk is how we protect our customers, Mercury, and the broader financial ecosystem. You'll join Fraud Operations, part of the Fraud & Disputes organization. The team investigates and prevents fraud across every Mercury product, and works hand in hand with Risk Strategy, Product, Engineering, Compliance, and our bank partners. Our investigators, Fraud Enablement team, and BPO partners handle the volume. This role makes sure that when something goes wrong, or when a regulator or bank partner asks hard questions, we respond quickly, consistently, and with evidence.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Role Summary

This is a senior individual contributor role for an investigator who thrives in the hardest, least defined problems in fraud. You will own fraud incident response from detection to postmortem across first-party and third-party fraud, write the memos and responses that our partners and auditors rely on, and be the operational voice of Fraud Operations in partner-bank conversations. You will lead Fraud Operations' response to audit and regulatory observations, and you will help Mercury get ready to operate as a bank, translating what examiners and partner banks expect into the processes, evidence, and documentation our teams need every day.

You don't need to be the deepest domain expert in every fraud typology. You need to be able to hold your own in an incident, ask the right questions, bring the right people in, and turn a messy channel full of data into a clear, defensible, and actionable narrative. You'll work closely with Fraud Investigations and Enablement, Risk Strategy, Compliance, Legal, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering.

What You'll Do

Lead fraud incident management

• Act as incident lead or operational DRI for fraud incidents across all Mercury products, including account takeover, card testing and BIN attacks, mule and ring activity, spikes in fraud behavior, and first-party fraud trends.

• Mobilize incident response, size impact, pull the right people from Fraud Investigations, Enablement, Strategy, Product, and Engineering, and keep everyone aligned on what we know, what we don't, and who owns what.

• Make or tee up decisions with a recommendation attached: containment, customer communication, reimbursement and credit decisions, account actions, and when to escalate.

• Run postmortems and retros for first-party and third-party fraud incidents: root cause, control gaps, remediation owners and dates, and track statuses of each.

• Spot patterns across incidents and turn them into durable fixes in alerts, rules, SOPs, product or tooling change requests, and training instead of one-off responses.

Write the memos and responses partners and auditors rely on

• Draft incident and retro memos for bank partners and internal risk governance: what happened, impact, root cause, controls in place, remediation plan, and timelines.

• Use AI tools to get from raw incident data to a strong first draft quickly, then verify every number and claim against source data before it leaves the team.

• Prepare accurate, concise responses to partner-bank questions, suspicious activity and investigation inquiries, and requests for information.

• Track open partner requests, commitments, and change-management items, and make sure Fraud Operations responds consistently and on time.

• Bring partner feedback and expectations back to Fraud Operations, Strategy, and Product so controls and processes are built with the partner in mind.

Support audit and exam response for the Fraud domain

title: Redwood Finance Automation Engineer, Romania
description:
Redwood Finance Automation Engineer, Romania
Contract: Duration being confirmed. Start: 15 November 2026. Location: Remote, for consultants based in Romania. Day rate: EUR 350 a day. Language: English.
The programme
An established organisation is automating its finance operations on Redwood Finance Automation. The work covers the record-to-report cycle: the period-end close, account reconciliation, journal processing and the reporting that follows, all connected to the organisation's ERP.
You will build what the solution design sets out. You will configure the close and reconciliation processes, build the integrations with the ERP and the systems around it, and carry each process through testing, go-live and early support.
What you will work on
Close processes built and configured end to end: task lists, dependencies, approvals and the automated steps between them. Automated account reconciliation, including matching rules and exception handling. Journal entry automation, from data preparation and validation through to posting in the ERP. Integration with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and other source systems, through standard connectors, file and API interfaces. Intercompany, accrual and reclassification steps automated alongside the close. Workflow logic in REL or JavaScript where the standard designer does not meet the requirement. Unit and integration testing, defect fixing, and support through user acceptance testing. Promotion between environments, cutover and hypercare. Technical documentation and handover to the support team.
What you bring
